Voat is already starting to suffer from a similar problem to Reddit in that we tend to naturally upvote things that are already upvoted for the simple reason that the software biases what's seen towards what's already been upvoted which results in it getting upvoted even more ultimately making it difficult for new posts to "overcome" it. Ultimately you end up with a frontpage that remains relatively static even though the amount of content being contributed, including plenty of quality stuff, is actually vast.

I think a simple and fun way to combat this would be to have a wildcard slot (or two) ordered prominently on the frontpage. The submissions here are not sorted based on votes but just random picks from all material submitted within the past 24 hours. The only filter would be to not display wildcard submissions to a user from subs that user is explicitly blocking. Wildcard NSFW stuff could be an opt-in toggle. Incidentally this would also help expose people to some smaller subverses they're not familiar with. The entire feature could include an opt-out option on the user page.

Men are 50% more likely to get esophageal cancer than 30 years ago

One possible explanation for increasing prevalence of esophageal and head/neck cancers in men is that Human Papilloma Virus is a known virus that causes cancer. In the case of females, HPV causes cervical cancer.

Here's a recently published article that shows that HPV is a cause of cancer of the esophagus. The conclusion of the authors is arguably dependent upon the location of the patient.

J Gastrointest Oncol. 2015 Jun;6(3):287-95. doi: 10.3978/j.issn.2078-6891.2015.001. Human papillomavirus tumor infection in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Ludmir EB1, Stephens SJ1, Palta M1, Willett CG1, Czito BG1. he association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) has been recognized for over three decades. Recently, multiple meta-analyses have drawn upon existing literature to assess the strength of the HPV-ESCC linkage. Here, we review these analyses and attempt to provide a clinically-relevant overview of HPV infection in ESCC. HPV-ESCC detection rates are highly variable across studies. Geographic location likely accounts for a majority of the variation in HPV prevalence, with high-incidence regions including Asia reporting significantly higher HPV-ESCC infection rates compared with low-incidence regions such as Europe, North America, and Oceania. Based on our examination of existing data, the current literature does not support the notion that HPV is a prominent carcinogen in ESCC. We conclude that there is no basis to change the current clinical approach to ESCC patients with respect to tumor HPV status.

It's a possibility, but I still have problems with the sex ratio. Females, of course, have cervixes, but I still don't see why cases of esophageal cancer due to HPV should be sparing of females just because they have another 'target' organ.

HPV spread is likely by direct contact. There is probably a difference in sexual behavior. Women may be less likely to spread HPV by oral contact. While men might be getting HPV through oral contact. This is speculative but logical. I'm sure that someone has assessed the contagion risk and the HPV subtypes.
